welcome.title: Comparing lanes
welcome.text: Lanes of one gel or several, side by side: their profiles, their purity, their bands matched by molecular weight. A short tour of the header and the panels; leave it at any time with <kbd>Esc</kbd>.

steps.title: Add lanes
steps.text: Pick a gel, tick its lanes, then Add Selected. Repeat for the lanes of other gels: they all go into this comparison.

steps.title: One assay at a time
steps.text: Lanes of different assays (an SDS-PAGE, an anti-HCP western) are never drawn on one axis: this switch shows one assay's lanes, the line under the header lists the others. Save keeps them all.

steps.title: MW tolerance
steps.text: How close, in %, two bands' molecular weights must be to share a row of the Band Comparison table and of the CSV export. 5 % by default, from 1 to 20.

steps.title: Scale the profiles
steps.text: How the overlaid profiles are scaled: Raw as measured, for equal loads; Total Lane, each lane summing to 100 %, when loads differ; Max Peak, each lane's tallest peak at 100 %, to compare shapes.

steps.title: The lanes, panel by panel
steps.text: On top, one card per lane: drag a card to reorder. Then the lanes side by side or cropped from their gels, the overlaid profiles or the readout's chart, a band's detail, and the Band Comparison table, with Avg purity on a purity assay.

steps.title: Save the comparison
steps.text: A name, an optional description, and whether every user may open it. It keeps the lanes in their order and the view: normalization, MW tolerance, axis, POI only. A saved comparison can be saved again as a new copy.

steps.title: Export and report
steps.text: Export CSV: every band of the lanes of the assay shown. Report: Word, Excel or PowerPoint, with the lanes' gels, the purity chart and the band comparison; save the comparison first.
